items.name: Readability
items.evidence: The new window() methods have JSDoc, the names say what they do (windowSql, windowChunks, buildWindowSpec), and the formatting matches the existing dialect code. The only single-letter name is the `w` loop variable, which is allowed. The `spec as WindowSpec` cast hides that strings are accepted, but that is minor.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: The spec builder (buildWindowSpec) is shared, but the whole window() body is copied five times: name validation, the SelectionProxyHandler callback and the push. There is no shared assertValidWindowName. window.ts sits in sql/expressions, not sql/functions as the convention asks.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: Empty and whitespace-only names are rejected as required. However, window() accepts `WindowSpec | string` and then does `spec: spec as WindowSpec`, so a string spec reaches buildWindowSpec as if it were a spec object. That is unvalidated and type-unsafe.

items.name: Public API additions are additive and consistent across dialects
items.name_zh: 公共 API 新增保持向后兼容且各方言一致
items.evidence: The change only adds things. Each *SelectConfig gets an optional `windows?`, and the WINDOW clause is emitted only when `windows.length > 0`, so queries without windows produce the same SQL. All five dialects get the same window() method, 'window' is added to the excluded set-operator methods, and no existing export or signature changed.
